basic_details.job_title: AUD Recruitment 2026 – Apply Online for 3 Project Research Scientist, Project Technical Support and More Posts
basic_details.short_information: The School of Human Studies at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University Delhi (AUD) has invited applications for three temporary posts, one each of Project Research Scientist-II (Non-Medical), Project Technical Support-I and Project Technical Support-II, under an ICMR-funded project. Each post is for six months, extendable, with remuneration as per ICMR norms. A postgraduate degree with minimum 55% marks is required and the upper age limit is 35 years. Applications go by email to [email protected], and the last date has been extended to 11 November 2026.

qualification.details: Prior experience in funded research projects, preferably in areas related to behavioural addiction, clinical psychology, cognitive neuroscience/neuropsychology, neurofeedback, and EEG data acquisition and analysis. Experience in experimental design and programming using EPrime and/or PsychoPy. Familiarity with quantitative and qualitative research methods, systematic literature reviews (SLRs), and meta-analysis. Ability to design and implement experimental paradigms and undertake data collection, analysis, interpretation, and research report writing. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and statistical or qualitative analysis software, such as SPSS, R, MATLAB, and NVivo. Strong academic writing, communication, coordination, and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and meet project deadlines.

how_to_apply: Email the application to [email protected]. The notice also allows submission using the link https://forms.gle/JRCCXnz4tGe2SYpx9 ("by email and/or using link"), on or before the deadline.

Write the subject line for the post applied for: "Application for Project Research Scientist-II. Non-Medical– ICMR Project", "Application for Project Technical Support-I– ICMR Project" or "Application for Project Technical Support-II– ICMR Project".
Attach a detailed CV including contact details (mobile number and email ID) and the names and contact details of two referees.
Attach a one-page Statement of Interest (up to 500 words) explaining the applicant's suitability for the project.
For Project Research Scientist-II (Non-Medical) only, also attach up to two publications or a relevant published writing sample in English (approximately 2,000 – 4,000 words).
Submit by 11 November 2026. Incomplete applications and applications containing plagiarized writing samples will be summarily rejected.
One-page Statement of Interest (up to 500 words)
Up to two publications or a published writing sample in English (Project Research Scientist-II (Non-Medical) only)
important_instructions: The University/School reserves the right to amend, reschedule, cancel, suspend, or withdraw the recruitment process, in part or in full, without assigning any reason. The decision is final and no appeal will be entertained. Expenditure on project-related travel, photocopying and stationery shall be reimbursed in accordance with AUD norms. The selected candidate must be willing to join immediately. In any dispute or ambiguity during the selection process, the decision of the University is final and binding. Updates on candidature appear on the University website, https://aud.delhi.gov.in/. For queries, email [email protected] with a copy to [email protected], using the subject line: Query Regarding ICMR Project Recruitment.

content_sections.heading: About the Project
content_sections.text: AUD is a public university of the Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, established under the Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University Delhi Act, 2007. The three posts serve the ICMR-funded D-RESeT project on digital addiction among university students in Delhi NCR. The notice names Dr. Pratima, Principal Investigator and Associate Professor, School of Human Studies, as the contact person.

content_sections.heading: Vacancy Details
content_sections.text: The notice invites applications for 3 posts in total. Category-wise break-up is not printed.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: All three posts have an upper age limit of 35 years. The notice prints no age cut-off date and no age relaxation. Each post needs a postgraduate degree with a minimum of 55% marks at the postgraduate level. Prior experience in funded research projects, preferably in areas related to behavioural addiction, clinical psychology, cognitive neuroscience/neuropsychology, neurofeedback, and EEG data acquisition and analysis. Experience in experimental design and programming using EPrime and/or PsychoPy. Familiarity with quantitative and qualitative research methods, systematic literature reviews (SLRs), and meta-analysis. Ability to design and implement experimental paradigms and undertake data collection, analysis, interpretation, and research report writing. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and statistical or qualitative analysis software, such as SPSS, R, MATLAB, and NVivo. Strong academic writing, communication, coordination, and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and meet project deadlines. Prior experience in research projects, preferably in the areas of behavioural addiction, clinical psychology, or psychophysiology. Familiarity with quantitative and/or qualitative research methods, including literature reviews, research instrument development, and data collection. Proficiency in MS Word, MS Excel, and statistical or qualitative data analysis software such as SPSS, NVivo, or equivalent tools. Good academic writing, communication, and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and meet project deadlines. Prior experience in research projects, preferably in areas related to behavioural addiction, yogic sciences, mindfulness-based interventions, or behavioural science laboratory research. Familiarity with quantitative and/or qualitative research methods, including literature reviews, research instrument development, and data collection. content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: Remuneration for all three posts is "as per ICMR norms"; the notice prints no amount. Each post is purely temporary and co-terminus with the project. The duration is six months, extendable based on performance and requirements. Based on performance review, the contract can be terminated on 15 days' notice anytime during the term. The services of a selected candidate may also be terminated if performance is found unsatisfactory, in accordance with the applicable terms and conditions of engagement.

content_sections.heading: AUD Recruitment 2026 Job Description
content_sections.text: For each post the notice says the project requires a self-motivated candidate with strong communication and coordination skills to support the successful execution of project objectives. The key responsibilities are listed below. Undertake primary and secondary research, including literature reviews, secondary data analysis, and the systematic organization and documentation of research materials. Conduct systematic literature reviews and meta-analyses, as required, and assist in designing and implementing experimental paradigms. Coordinate and support data collection and field research activities, including fieldwork planning, logistics, and liaison with relevant stakeholders. Assist in questionnaire development, data transcription, compilation, entry, coding, and quantitative and qualitative data analysis. Support the preparation of research outputs, including manuscripts for academic journals, research reports, policy briefs, presentations, and other project-related documentation. Maintain research records, project documentation, and data in an organized and systematic manner. Coordinate project-related logistics and facilitate communication among team members and external stakeholders. Undertake other research-related responsibilities assigned by the Project Team in accordance with the project objectives. faq.question: Q1. How many posts are open in AUD Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Three posts are open, one each of Project Research Scientist-II (Non-Medical), Project Technical Support-I and Project Technical Support-II.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply?
faq.answer: The last date has been extended to 11 November 2026. The earlier date was 06 November 2026.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification required?
faq.answer: A postgraduate degree (MA/MSc) in Psychology, Neuropsychology, Applied Psychology, Cognitive Sciences, Social Sciences or an allied discipline with minimum 55% marks at postgraduate level. Project Research Scientist-II (Non-Medical) also lists MPhil/PhD in a relevant discipline as an additional qualification.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit?
faq.answer: The upper age limit is 35 years for all three posts.

faq.question: Q5. What is the pay?
faq.answer: Remuneration is as per ICMR norms for all three posts. The notice prints no amount.

faq.question: Q6. How do I apply?
faq.answer: Email the CV, a Statement of Interest and, for Project Research Scientist-II (Non-Medical), writing samples to [email protected] with the post-specific subject line. The notice also names the Google Form link https://forms.gle/JRCCXnz4tGe2SYpx9.

faq.question: Q7. Is this a permanent job?
faq.answer: No. Each post is purely temporary and co-terminus with the project, for six months, extendable based on performance and requirements.

faq.question: Q8. Is travel allowance paid for the interview?
faq.answer: No TA/DA is payable for attending the interview. Project-related travel, photocopying and stationery expenditure is reimbursed in accordance with AUD norms.

faq.question: Q9. What should the email subject line be?
faq.answer: Use "Application for" followed by the post name and "– ICMR Project", for example "Application for Project Technical Support-I– ICMR Project".

faq.question: Q10. How will candidates be selected?
faq.answer: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted, and the interview schedule will be published on the University website and emailed to them.
